Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)

Required findings: Significant daily pain causing clinically meaningful functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND unremitting radicular pain to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam demonstrates ANY of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor weakness of biceps or triceps, reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., positive Spurling's maneuver), OR unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings

MRI or CT of the cervical spine shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with symptoms and exam, caused by herniated disc (including recurrent disc), synovial or arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes
Plain cervical spine x‑rays (including flexion/extension lateral views) have been performed

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following for a minimum of six (6) weeks (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs; provider‑directed exercise program (PT, chiropractic, osteopathic, or physician‑prescribed); epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block at the same level(s)
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)

Documented nicotine‑free status: either never‑smoker or abstinent from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery, verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range

Symptoms include ANY of: upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting, hand clumsiness); gait disturbance; new‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; frequent falls

Physical exam demonstrates ANY of: abnormal grip‑and‑release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, myelopathic hand
MRI or CT of the cervical spine shows findings concordant with the individual's symptoms and exam, caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis

Non-Indications: Absence of the required symptom severity or functional impairment for radiculopathy (e.g., mild intermittent pain without disability)
Lack of any concordant objective physical‑exam findings for radiculopathy when imaging is not supportive
Failure to complete the mandated minimum trial of at least two conservative modalities for six weeks (unless medically contraindicated)
Missing or non‑concordant MRI/CT evidence of neural compression at the proposed surgical level
No plain cervical spine flexion/extension x‑rays performed when required for radiculopathy
Active tobacco use without documented abstinence ≥6 weeks or without objective cotinine verification
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
For myelopathy, symptoms or exam findings that do not meet any of the listed criteria, or imaging that does not demonstrate cord compression or stenosis
Prior cervical fusion at the same level (procedure would be considered revision, not initial primary ACDF)
Important criteria & exceptions: Objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) must be performed within a clinically appropriate timeframe (typically within 30 days of surgery) to verify nicotine‑free status
Conservative therapy requirement may be waived only if the patient has a documented contraindication to the therapy (e.g., allergy to NSAIDs, inability to tolerate PT)
Plain cervical spine flexion/extension lateral views are required for radiculopathy to assess segmental stability before fusion
Behavioral health assessment must explicitly state that no significant unmanaged mental or substance‑use disorder is present
If both radiculopathy and myelopathy criteria are met, the more restrictive set of requirements (radiculopathy) applies
Documentation required: Comprehensive history and physical note documenting symptom severity, functional impairment, and disability
Neurological examination note detailing specific objective findings (sensory deficits, motor weakness, reflex changes, Spurling's maneuver, grip‑and‑release, gait assessment, etc.)

Cervical spine MRI report (or CT if MRI contraindicated) with level‑specific description of neural compression, including cause (herniated disc, cyst, stenosis, osteophytes) for radiculopathy or cord compression/stenosis for myelopathy
Plain cervical spine radiographs including flexion and extension lateral views
Records of prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, or NSAIDs prescribed for ≥6 weeks
Physical therapy, chiropractic, osteopathic, or physician‑directed exercise program notes confirming ≥6 weeks of participation
Procedure reports for epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) (if used as part of the conservative trial)
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming absence of unmanaged significant mental or substance‑use disorder
Smoking history and cessation documentation, plus objective cotinine test result (laboratory report) showing normal range
If applicable, prior cervical surgery operative report to confirm this is an initial primary procedure
